The Police Sub-Inspector, Rajagopalanagar P.S., Bangalore City, has filed charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable U/s.498-A and 307 of IPC in their crime No.144/2016.
2.

The factual matrix of the case is that:-

1

The accused married-informant.Smt. Vanitha, who divorced from her first husband,
and she had two children from her first husband, and there was a quarrel between accused and the informant, and in this regard complaint has been lodged on 22.02.2016 by the informant at Kunigal P.S., and after the advise of police accused and complainant started residing at Hegganahalli, within the limits of Rajagopalanagar P.S., Bangalore, accused being the husband of complainant-Smt.
Vanitha and by enraging with lodging of complaint subjected her to physical and mental cruelty, and on 25.02.2016 at 9.30 p.m. accused picked up quarrel with the informant by assaulting abusing in filthy language, and with intention and knowledge to kill the complainant made her to fall on the ground, and at that time accused forcibly put mosquito repellent in her mouth, made her to consume, attempted to kill her and thereby the accused has committed the offences as alleged against him.

3.The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the jurisdictional VII Addl., CMM.,
Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing charge sheet copy to the accused.
The same was numbered as SC No.1739/2018.
4.The charge was framed and read over to the accused on 1.8.2022 for the offences punishable U/s.498A and 307 of IPC.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
5.The prosecution has examined in all four witnesses as PW.1 to PW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P5 and identifies MO1.

In spite of sufficient opportunities provided to the prosecution by issuing summons, warrant and proclamation for securing CW.4, but the concerned police failed to secure the said witness and in view of the same the evidence of CW.4 taken as nil by rejecting the prayer of the prosecution.
Further the prosecution has not taken any steps to secure the witnesses CW.2 and CW.3, in view of the same dropping of evidence of CW.2 and CW.3 remained intact.

The witnesses CW.2 and CW.3 have not not been examined by the prosecution due to failure of concerned police to secure the said witnesses and keep present before the Court for the purpose of evidence.

So the evidence of prosecution was taken as closed with an opportunity to examine the said witness CW.2 and CW.3, if the said witnesses were secured and produced by the concerned police before the Court for examination before conclusion of the trial.
6.After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused on 8.2.2024 as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him, and not chosen to lead defense evidence.
However, the accused got marked documents at Ex.D.1 on his behalf 7.Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.

8.The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused being husband of complainant/victim while residing at Hegganahalli, within the Rajagopalangara Ps vs Suresh Kumar on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102851662/
2 limits of Rajagopalanagar P.S., Bangalore, subjected complainant-Smt.Vanitha to physical and mental cruelty and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.498-A of IPC ?
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused being husband of the complainant while residing at at Hegganahalli, within the limits of Rajagopalanagar P.S., Bangalore, subjected complainant-Smt.Vanitha to physical and mental cruelty and on 25.02.2016 at 9.30 p.m. accused picked up quarrel with the informant by assaulting abusing in filthy language, and with intention and knowledge to kill the complainant made her fall on the ground, and at that time accused forcibly put mosquito repellent in her mouth, made her to consume,
attempted to kill her and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.307 of IPC?
3. What Order?

9.This Court findings on the above points are as hereunder:
Point No.1: In the Negative Point No.2: In the Negative Point No.3: As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Points No.1 and 2: Both the points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.

It is the case of the prosecution that the accused married- informant.Smt. Vanitha, who divorced from her first husband, and she had two children from her first husband, and there was a quarrel between accused and the informant, and in this regard complaint has been lodged on 22.02.2016 by the informant at Kunigal P.S., and after the advise of police accused and complainant started residing at Hegganahalli, within the limits of Rajagopalanagar P.S., Bangalore, accused being the husband of complainant-Smt. Vanitha and by enraging with lodging of complaint subjected her to physical and mental cruelty, and on 25.02.2016 at 9.30 p.m. accused picked up quarrel with the informant by assaulting abusing in filthy language, and with intention and knowledge to kill the complainant made her to fall on the ground, and at that time accused forcibly put mosquito repellent in her mouth, made her to consume, attempted to kill her and thereby the accused has committed the offences as alleged against him.
11.Among the 4 witnesses examined by the prosecution
, the prime witness PW.1 Smt. Vanitha being the informant and victim, deposed that her marriage was solemnized with one Gangadhara in the year 2007.
Out of the said wedlock she blessed with two children.
She was residing at Hegganahalli Cross, Sunkadakatte, Bangalore, at that time she came in contact with accused, she was speaking to accused through phone.
One day when she was traveling to Hegadathihalli of Kunigal Taluk, the accused accompanied her at Hulukoppa Village.
She stayed with accused in his farm house.

Her Rajagopalangara Ps vs Suresh Kumar on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102851662/
3
husband came to know about her stay with the accused in his farm house.
She confessed before her husband regarding her stay with accused.
Her husband started quarreling with her, thereafter the accused started to stay with her even in the presence of her husband.
Her husband was watching the same for a period of six months, thereafter accused arranged another house and she went along with the accused.
Her children were staying with her husband.
Her marriage was solemnized with the accused.
She got divorce from her previous husband.
It was the second marriage to the accused with her.
The accused wanted to pay Rs.5,00,000/- to his first wife.
The accused insisted her to pay Rs.5,00,000/-.
The brother of the accused refused to help him, as he wanted to stay with her.
Therefore the accused maintained distance from her.
Once she went to the native place of accused and warned him to pull thali chain if he is not interested to continue relationship with her.
The accused pulled her mangalya chain.
She came to Bangalore.
Later the accused also came with her to Bangalore.
One day at about 8.00 p.m. the accused pulled her hair, assaulted and abused her in filthy language.
The neighboring resident by name Girija locked from outside to prevent the accused running away from her house.
The accused with intention to kill her forcibly put the allout liquid in her mouth, she started shouting.
The neighboring resident and Girija shifted her to Lakshmi Hospital, Sunkadakatte.
She gave complaint as per Ex.P1 when she was under treatment.
The jurisdictional police drawn the mahazar in the place of occurrence.
She identifies MO1 allout bottle seized and the same is marked as MO1
Her marriage with first husband ended in divorce in the year 2015.
She gave photographs to the police to prove the relationship with the accused.

In the year 2020 she got married with another person, and a complaint was filed against him in Kunigal P.S.,
alleging that her money and gold is being stolen by him.
The said case has been dismissed.
She also gave another complaint in Huliyurudurga P.S., Crime No.22/2017 as per EX.D1.
Her name in Ex.D1 complaint shown as Vanitha W/ o Gangadhara.
In the complaint filed against her another husband by name Harish alleged that first wife of said Harish and his mother-in-law are assaulting her.
The said case is settled amicably.
Girija who locked the door is none other than the friend of accused.
She has not remembered the date of alleged offences committed by the accused.
She did not give further statement before the Police.
Consumption of all-out poison has been denied by the learned counsel for the accused.
Demand for Rs.5,00,000/- and alleged physical and mental harassment meted out by her has been denied by the learned counsel for the accused.

12.PW.2 Santhosh Ram, PSI, Rajagopalanagar P.S., Bangalore, received Ex.P1 complaint in Lakshmi Multispeciality Hospital in the present Medical Officer, registered the case and forwarded the FIR to the jurisdictional Magistrate as per Ex.P2.
Ex.P3 is the MLC Report, Ex.P4 is the spot mahazar drawn by PW.2, seized MO1 all-out liquid bottle.
Recorded statements of witnesses, collected discharge summary marked as Ex.P5, and handed over further investigation to CW.7.
According to PW.2 the informant victim had not produced any documents to show that she was legally wedded wife of accused.
He did not collect documents to show that the informant is divorced wife of one Gangadhara.
He is not aware about the complaint filed by informant against one Harish.
He is aware about the complaint filed by informant against the accused in Kunigal P.S., In Ex.P1 complaint date of forcible consumption of all-out liquid poison by PW.1 has not been mentioned.
Notice was not given to spot mahazar witnesses to be present at the time of seizure of MO1 all-out liquid bottle.
He denies that a false case is registered against the accused to help the informant.

Rajagopalangara Ps vs Suresh Kumar on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102851662/
4 13.PW.3

Dr. B. R. Prabhakar, Medical Officer, Lakshim Multi-Specialty Hospital deposed that on 24.2.2016 at 11.45 p.m. informant Vanitha was admitted to the hospital with history of consumption of mosquito poison.
Stomach wash was collected and handed over to the police.
Lakshmi Multi- Specialty Hospital issued MLC report marked as Ex.
P5. He did not see the FSL report i.e., stomach wash contents examination report.
14.PW,4 H.P. Sharath Kumar, conducted further investigation and filed charge sheet against the accused.

Ex.P5 MLC report reveals that the informant Vanitha was admitted to Lakshmi Multi-specialty Hospital, Bangalore, on 24.02.2016 at 11.45 p.m. and she has been discharged from the said hospital on 25.2.2016 at 11.00 a.m.
She was admitted to the Hospital with history of consumption of mosquito repellent liquid at her residence.
On examination of PW.1 Medical Officer at Lakshmi Multi-specialty Hospital, found that the informant was conscious and oriented.
She was treated with antibiotic and other supportive medicines, and discharged from the Hospital.
Stomach wash collection has not been mentioned in Ex.P5 discharge summary.

Absolutely there is no documentary evidence to establish that the informant forcibly consumed mosquito repellent liquid,
there is no FSL report to prove the alleged offences against the accused.
The valid marriage between the informant and accused has not been established with available evidence on record.
Offence alleged to have been committed by the accused punishable U/s.498A and 307 of IPC has not been established by the prosecution.
Accordingly, I answer Points No.1 and 2 in the Negative.
15. Point No.3:

In view of answer of court on points No.1 to 4, this court pass the following:-
ORDER Acting U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.498A and 307 of IPC .
The bail and surety bonds of accused stand canceled.
MO1 being worthless shall be destroyed after appeal period is over.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer corrected by me and then pronounced in open Court on this the 14th day of March, 2024)
(Manjunatha) XLV Addl.
City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru.
MANJUNATH RAMA NAIK  RAMA NAIK Date: 2024.03.18
